text:
Kai: Running multi-GPU sweep (A100 / H100 / L40S) for attention kernels. Saw a weird throughput drop with paged-flash + prefetch on L40S when batch size is in the 12-16 range and seq_len >= 2048. Full run stats uploaded.

Alex: Which commit/branch?

Kai: main@c2f4b9e (recent kernel selector tweaks + prefetch window change). Repro command: 
```bash
./bench/run_attention_sweep.sh --models gpt2-medium --devices A100,H100,L40S --seqs 512,1024,2048,4096 --bsz 4,8,12,16,24 --variants fused paged flash paged-prefetch
```

Maria: Is this 1) a scheduling/queueing artifact across GPUs, or 2) a kernel-level regression?

Kai: Profiling points to a spike in CUDA memcpy wait time on L40S (~30-60ms extra per step) + KV-cache churn at the same bsz/seq combo. Flamegraphs show a long tail in `kv_cache::evict` overlapping with `paged_prefetch_worker`.

TJ: I ran the same subset on a single L40S and couldn't reproduce at bsz=12 for seq=2048. Multi-GPU cross-node run reproduced it reliably. Maybe an inter-GPU comms pattern triggers evictions? :thinking_face:

Alex: BenchBot, where are the raw flamegraphs/logs?

BenchBot: Results uploaded: s3://redwood-bench/3776543210/ (summary.csv, per-gpu-trace.zip, flamegraphs/)

Kai: Key numbers from summary.csv (avg tokens/s):
- A100, seq=2048, bsz=8: fused=4100, paged=3950, paged-prefetch=4020
- L40S, seq=2048, bsz=8: fused=2200, paged=2150, paged-prefetch=2175
- L40S, seq=2048, bsz=12: fused=2100, paged=1780, paged-prefetch=1620  <-- big drop
- H100, seq=2048, bsz=12: paged-prefetch=3800 (no drop)

Maria: That's a >20% drop between fused and paged-prefetch on L40S at bsz=12. Suggests a memory-bandwidth/KV contention specific to paged-prefetch path on that device.

Alex: Any meminfo / nvprof slices?

Kai: Pasted a short nvprof slice below (truncated):
```
Device: L40S  CUDA 12.3
TimeSlice  | Kernel                         | GPU_time(ms) | Memcpy_wait(ms)
step 512   | flash_paged_prefetch_kernel    | 4.2          | 0.6
step 513   | flash_paged_prefetch_kernel    | 4.3          | 45.1  <-- big memcpy stall
step 514   | flash_paged_prefetch_kernel    | 4.2          | 0.5
```

TJ: That 45ms memcpy wait lines up with inter-GPU `alltoall` windows. Are we batching small collectives at that bsz? Could be fragmentation in NCCL buffers when prefetch allocs align badly.

Maria: Hypothesis: prefetch spawns async transfers that race with KV eviction paths. On L40S the prefetch window + smaller bus topology -> larger stalls.

Alex: Repro steps to validate: 1) disable prefetch and run same sweep; 2) tighten the prefetch window to <= 64 tokens; 3) run with `--no-kv-evict` (dev flag) to see if eviction is the root cause. Kai can you run 1 & 3 on the same multi-GPU cluster?

Kai: Running now: disabling prefetch eliminates the drop (paged w/o prefetch at bsz=12 on L40S -> 2090 tokens/s). With `--no-kv-evict` + prefetch I see 2065 tokens/s (preliminary). So eviction + prefetch interaction seems likely.

TJ: Good signal. Next: bisect recent prefetch change range? Could be the commit that introduced async prefetch cancellation/cleanup.

Alex: I'll take a bisect on the prefetch patch range (PR#4226..PR#4272) tomorrow. If it's a correctness/ordering bug we can hotfix the prefetch cancellation to await outstanding transfers before triggering eviction.

Maria: Also add a guard in selector: avoid choosing paged-prefetch for L40S for bsz >= 12 and seq >= 2048 until we confirm. Fail-open to fused or paged-no-prefetch. Safer to avoid regressions in prod.

Kai: Agreed. Added a temporary kernel-policy patch to canary: `if device.family==L40S and bsz>=12 and seq>=2048 -> prefer fused`

BenchBot: Canary rollout: 10% of realtime traffic routed to fallback policy. Observability dashboards updated.

Alex: Thanks. After I finish bisect I'll link the offending commit and propose patch. Good detective work team :eyes: 

Kai: Leaving logs and a short PR draft in the bench ticket. Will post updates here once bisect narrows it down.

Maria: Nice. If bisect points to kernel ordering, consider adding perf regression tests to CI for the bsz=12/seq=2048 L40S case. Repro is fast enough (~30m).

TJ: I'll add CI job draft after Alex's bisect.

Alex: ETA bisect results EOD tomorrow.

Kai: Cool, thanks all.
